quotes.text: Joseph, son of David, do not fear to take Mary as your wife, for that which is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
quotes.speaker: An angel of the Lord
quotes.context: Speaking to Joseph in a dream after he had resolved to divorce Mary quietly.

quotes.text: Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star when it rose and have come to worship him.
quotes.speaker: The wise men (Magi) from the east
quotes.context: Arriving in Jerusalem looking for the newborn king, which troubled Herod and all Jerusalem.

quotes.text: Go and search diligently for the child, and when you have found him, bring me word, that I too may come and worship him.
quotes.speaker: King Herod
quotes.context: Secretly sending the wise men to Bethlehem; he actually intended to destroy the child.

quotes.text: Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and remain there until I tell you, for Herod is about to search for the child, to destroy him.
quotes.speaker: An angel of the Lord
quotes.context: Warning Joseph in a dream after the wise men left.

quotes.text: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
quotes.speaker: John the Baptist (Jesus later preaches the same words in 4:17)
quotes.context: Preaching in the wilderness of Judea.

quotes.text: You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
quotes.speaker: John the Baptist
quotes.context: To the many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism; he tells them to bear fruit in keeping with repentance.

quotes.text: I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?
quotes.speaker: John the Baptist
quotes.context: Trying to prevent Jesus from being baptized by him at the Jordan. Jesus replies, 'Let it be so now... to fulfill all righteousness.'

quotes.text: This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.
quotes.speaker: A voice from heaven (God the Father)
quotes.context: At Jesus' baptism, as the Spirit of God descended like a dove. (At the Transfiguration the voice adds 'listen to him'.)

quotes.text: If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become loaves of bread.
quotes.speaker: The tempter (the devil)
quotes.context: The first temptation, after Jesus had fasted forty days and forty nights in the wilderness.

quotes.text: All these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me.
quotes.speaker: The devil
quotes.context: The third temptation, on a very high mountain, showing Jesus all the kingdoms of the world. Jesus answers, 'Be gone, Satan!'

quotes.text: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Calling Simon Peter and Andrew as they cast a net into the Sea of Galilee.

quotes.text: Lord, if you will, you can make me clean.
quotes.speaker: A leper
quotes.context: Kneeling before Jesus as he came down from the mountain after the Sermon on the Mount.

quotes.text: Lord, I am not worthy to have you come under my roof, but only say the word, and my servant will be healed.
quotes.speaker: A centurion in Capernaum
quotes.context: Asking Jesus to heal his paralyzed servant, explaining that he too is a man under authority.

quotes.text: Truly, I tell you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Marveling at the centurion who asked him only to say the word to heal his servant.

quotes.text: Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Answering a scribe who said, 'Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.'

quotes.text: Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To a disciple who asked to first go and bury his father.

quotes.text: Save us, Lord; we are perishing.
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: Waking Jesus, who was asleep in the boat during a great storm on the sea.

quotes.text: What sort of man is this, that even winds and sea obey him?
quotes.speaker: The disciples (the men in the boat)
quotes.context: After Jesus rebuked the winds and the sea and there was a great calm.

quotes.text: What have you to do with us, O Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?
quotes.speaker: The two demon-possessed men
quotes.context: Meeting Jesus in the country of the Gadarenes; the demons then beg to be sent into the herd of pigs.

quotes.text: Take heart, my son; your sins are forgiven.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To a paralytic brought to him on a bed; some scribes thought, 'This man is blaspheming.'

quotes.text: Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?
quotes.speaker: The Pharisees
quotes.context: Asking Jesus' disciples while Jesus reclined at table in Matthew's house.

quotes.text: Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick... I desire mercy, and not sacrifice.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Answering the Pharisees who objected to him eating with tax collectors and sinners at Matthew's house.

quotes.text: Why do we and the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?
quotes.speaker: The disciples of John the Baptist
quotes.context: Jesus answers that the wedding guests cannot mourn while the bridegroom is with them.

quotes.text: If I only touch his garment, I will be made well.
quotes.speaker: A woman who had suffered from a discharge of blood for twelve years
quotes.context: Said to herself as she came up behind Jesus, on his way to the ruler's house, and touched the fringe of his garment.

quotes.text: Go away, for the girl is not dead but sleeping.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: At the ruler's house among the flute players and the noisy crowd, who laughed at him. He then took the girl by the hand and she arose.

quotes.text: Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?
quotes.speaker: John the Baptist (through his disciples)
quotes.context: Sent from prison after hearing about the deeds of the Christ.

quotes.text: Look, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.
quotes.speaker: The Pharisees
quotes.context: When the hungry disciples plucked heads of grain in the grainfields on the Sabbath.

quotes.text: Can this be the Son of David?
quotes.speaker: The crowds
quotes.context: Amazed after Jesus healed a blind and mute demon-oppressed man. The Pharisees responded that he cast out demons by Beelzebul.

quotes.text: It is only by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, that this man casts out demons.
quotes.speaker: The Pharisees
quotes.context: After Jesus healed a blind and mute demon-oppressed man; Jesus answers that a house divided against itself will not stand.

quotes.text: Teacher, we wish to see a sign from you.
quotes.speaker: Some of the scribes and Pharisees
quotes.context: Jesus answers that no sign will be given to this evil and adulterous generation except the sign of the prophet Jonah.

quotes.text: Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: When told his mother and brothers were standing outside asking to speak to him; he pointed to his disciples.

quotes.text: Why do you speak to them in parables?
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: After the parable of the sower; Jesus says the secrets of the kingdom have been given to them but not to the crowds.

quotes.text: Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? How then does it have weeds? ... An enemy has done this.
quotes.speaker: The servants, then the master of the house (in the parable of the weeds)
quotes.context: In the parable, when the weeds appeared among the wheat. The master tells them to let both grow until the harvest.

quotes.text: Is not this the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary? And are not his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?
quotes.speaker: The people of Nazareth (Jesus' hometown synagogue)
quotes.context: Astonished and offended by his teaching. Jesus replies that a prophet is not without honor except in his hometown.

quotes.text: This is John the Baptist. He has been raised from the dead; that is why these miraculous powers are at work in him.
quotes.speaker: Herod the tetrarch (Herod Antipas)
quotes.context: Saying to his servants after hearing about the fame of Jesus, having already beheaded John.

quotes.text: It is not lawful for you to have her.
quotes.speaker: John the Baptist
quotes.context: Rebuking Herod the tetrarch for taking Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, which led to John's imprisonment.

quotes.text: Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a platter.
quotes.speaker: The daughter of Herodias
quotes.context: Prompted by her mother, after her dance pleased Herod at his birthday and he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.

quotes.text: We have only five loaves here and two fish.
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: When Jesus told them, 'You give them something to eat' before feeding the five thousand.

quotes.text: Take heart; it is I. Do not be afraid.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Walking on the sea toward the disciples' boat in the fourth watch of the night; they thought he was a ghost.

quotes.text: Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water.
quotes.speaker: Peter
quotes.context: When Jesus came walking on the sea. Peter walked on the water, then began to sink when he saw the wind and cried, 'Lord, save me.'

quotes.text: O you of little faith, why did you doubt?
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Catching Peter, who had begun to sink while walking on the water.

quotes.text: Truly you are the Son of God.
quotes.speaker: The disciples in the boat
quotes.context: Worshiping Jesus after he and Peter got into the boat and the wind ceased.

quotes.text: Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat.
quotes.speaker: Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem
quotes.context: Jesus answers by asking why they break the commandment of God (honor your father and mother) for the sake of their tradition.

quotes.text: Send her away, for she is crying out after us.
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: About the Canaanite woman in the district of Tyre and Sidon who begged Jesus to heal her daughter.

quotes.text: Yes, Lord, yet even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table.
quotes.speaker: The Canaanite woman
quotes.context: Answering Jesus' saying that it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs. He praises her great faith and heals her daughter.

quotes.text: Who do people say that the Son of Man is?
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To his disciples in the district of Caesarea Philippi; they answer John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah or one of the prophets. Then he asks, 'But who do you say that I am?'

quotes.text: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
quotes.speaker: Simon Peter
quotes.context: Answering Jesus' question 'But who do you say that I am?' at Caesarea Philippi.

quotes.text: And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Responding to Peter's confession that he is the Christ at Caesarea Philippi.

quotes.text: Far be it from you, Lord! This shall never happen to you.
quotes.speaker: Peter
quotes.context: Rebuking Jesus after he first foretold that he must suffer, be killed and be raised.

quotes.text: Get behind me, Satan! You are a hindrance to me. For you are not setting your mind on the things of God, but on the things of man.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To Peter, who had rebuked him for saying he must suffer and be killed.

quotes.text: Lord, it is good that we are here. If you wish, I will make three tents here, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.
quotes.speaker: Peter
quotes.context: At the Transfiguration, when Moses and Elijah appeared talking with Jesus.

quotes.text: This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased; listen to him.
quotes.speaker: A voice from the bright cloud (God the Father)
quotes.context: At the Transfiguration, while Peter was still speaking about making three tents. (Unlike at the baptism, this one adds 'listen to him'.)

quotes.text: Why could we not cast it out?
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: After Jesus healed the epileptic boy they had failed to heal. Jesus says it was their little faith; faith like a mustard seed can move a mountain.

quotes.text: Does your teacher not pay the tax?
quotes.speaker: The collectors of the two-drachma tax
quotes.context: Asking Peter in Capernaum. Jesus later sends Peter to find a shekel in a fish's mouth.

quotes.text: Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: Jesus calls a child to him and says that unless they turn and become like children they will never enter the kingdom.

quotes.text: Lord, how often will my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? As many as seven times?
quotes.speaker: Peter
quotes.context: Jesus answers 'seventy-seven times' and tells the parable of the unforgiving servant.

quotes.text: Have patience with me, and I will pay you everything.
quotes.speaker: The servant who owed ten thousand talents (and later his fellow servant, with nearly the same words)
quotes.context: In the parable of the unforgiving servant, begging the king not to sell him and his family.

quotes.text: Is it lawful to divorce one's wife for any cause?
quotes.speaker: The Pharisees
quotes.context: Testing Jesus in the region of Judea beyond the Jordan.

quotes.text: If such is the case of a man with his wife, it is better not to marry.
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: Reacting to Jesus' teaching on divorce; he responds about those who are eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom.

quotes.text: Teacher, what good deed must I do to have eternal life?
quotes.speaker: The rich young man
quotes.context: Jesus tells him to keep the commandments, then to sell what he possesses and follow him.

quotes.text: All these I have kept. What do I still lack?
quotes.speaker: The rich young man
quotes.context: After Jesus listed commandments such as do not murder, honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.

quotes.text: Who then can be saved?
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: Astonished after Jesus said it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom.

quotes.text: See, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have?
quotes.speaker: Peter
quotes.context: After the rich young man went away sorrowful. Jesus promises the twelve will sit on twelve thrones judging Israel.

quotes.text: These last worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.
quotes.speaker: The laborers hired first (in the parable)
quotes.context: Grumbling at the master of the house when everyone was paid a denarius.

quotes.text: Say that these two sons of mine are to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your kingdom.
quotes.speaker: The mother of the sons of Zebedee (James and John)
quotes.context: Kneeling before Jesus on the way up to Jerusalem; the other ten were indignant.

quotes.text: Even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To the twelve, after the ten were indignant at James and John's mother's request for places of honor.

quotes.text: Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!
quotes.speaker: Two blind men sitting by the roadside
quotes.context: As Jesus left Jericho; the crowd rebuked them, but they cried out all the more. (Two other blind men cry nearly the same in 9:27.)

quotes.text: Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!
quotes.speaker: The crowds
quotes.context: Going before and following Jesus as he rode into Jerusalem on a donkey.

quotes.text: This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.
quotes.speaker: The crowds
quotes.context: Answering 'Who is this?' as the whole city of Jerusalem was stirred up at the triumphal entry.

quotes.text: It is written, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer,' but you make it a den of robbers.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Driving out those who bought and sold in the temple and overturning the money-changers' tables.

quotes.text: Do you hear what these are saying?
quotes.speaker: The chief priests and the scribes
quotes.context: Indignant at children crying 'Hosanna to the Son of David!' in the temple. Jesus quotes 'Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies you have prepared praise.'

quotes.text: May no fruit ever come from you again!
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To a fig tree by the road with nothing on it but leaves, as he returned to Jerusalem hungry in the morning. It withered at once.

quotes.text: By what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority?
quotes.speaker: The chief priests and the elders of the people
quotes.context: Confronting Jesus while he taught in the temple. He answers with a question about John's baptism.

quotes.text: I go, sir.
quotes.speaker: The second son (in the parable of the two sons)
quotes.context: Told by his father to work in the vineyard; he said this but did not go.

quotes.text: They will respect my son... This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and have his inheritance.
quotes.speaker: The master of the vineyard, then the wicked tenants (in the parable)
quotes.context: After the tenants had beaten, killed and stoned the servants sent to collect the fruit.

quotes.text: The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes.
quotes.speaker: Jesus (quoting Psalm 118)
quotes.context: To the chief priests and elders after the parable of the wicked tenants.

quotes.text: Friend, how did you get in here without a wedding garment?
quotes.speaker: The king (in the parable of the wedding feast)
quotes.context: To a guest gathered from the roads who was not dressed for the feast; he is bound and cast into the outer darkness.

quotes.text: Tell us, then, what you think. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?
quotes.speaker: Disciples of the Pharisees, along with the Herodians
quotes.context: Trying to entangle Jesus in his words after flattering him as true and impartial.

quotes.text: Therefore render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: After asking whose likeness and inscription was on the denarius used for the tax.

quotes.text: In the resurrection, therefore, of the seven, whose wife will she be? For they all had her.
quotes.speaker: The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection
quotes.context: Testing Jesus with a woman who married seven brothers in turn.

quotes.text: You are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Answering the Sadducees' question about the woman married to seven brothers.

quotes.text: Teacher, which is the great commandment in the Law?
quotes.speaker: A lawyer (one of the Pharisees)
quotes.context: Testing Jesus after he had silenced the Sadducees.

quotes.text: The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet.
quotes.speaker: Jesus (quoting David in Psalm 110)
quotes.context: Asking the Pharisees how the Christ can be David's son if David calls him Lord. No one could answer.

quotes.text: You blind guides, straining out a gnat and swallowing a camel!
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: One of the woes against the scribes and Pharisees, who tithe mint, dill and cumin but neglect justice, mercy and faithfulness.

quotes.text: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often would I have gathered your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Lamenting over Jerusalem at the end of the woes against the scribes and Pharisees.

quotes.text: Truly, I say to you, there will not be left here one stone upon another that will not be thrown down.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: As the disciples pointed out the buildings of the temple.

quotes.text: Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the close of the age?
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: Asking Jesus privately as he sat on the Mount of Olives, which began the Olivet Discourse.

quotes.text: Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.
quotes.speaker: A cry at midnight (in the parable of the ten virgins)
quotes.context: When the delayed bridegroom finally came and the virgins trimmed their lamps.

quotes.text: Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.
quotes.speaker: The five foolish virgins
quotes.context: To the wise virgins when the bridegroom arrived at midnight.

quotes.text: Well done, good and faithful servant. You have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.
quotes.speaker: The master (in the parable of the talents)
quotes.context: To the servant who turned five talents into ten (and the same to the one who turned two into four).

quotes.text: Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow, and gathering where you scattered no seed, so I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground.
quotes.speaker: The servant who had received one talent
quotes.context: Settling accounts with his master; he is called wicked and slothful and cast into the outer darkness.

quotes.text: Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.
quotes.speaker: The King (the Son of Man)
quotes.context: In the final judgment, to the sheep on his right hand who fed, welcomed, clothed and visited him.

quotes.text: Not during the feast, lest there be an uproar among the people.
quotes.speaker: The chief priests and the elders
quotes.context: Plotting in the palace of Caiaphas to arrest Jesus by stealth and kill him.

quotes.text: Why this waste? For this could have been sold for a large sum and given to the poor.
quotes.speaker: The disciples
quotes.context: Indignant when a woman poured very expensive ointment on Jesus' head at Simon the leper's house in Bethany.

quotes.text: What will you give me if I deliver him over to you?
quotes.speaker: Judas Iscariot
quotes.context: To the chief priests, who paid him thirty pieces of silver.

quotes.text: Is it I, Rabbi?
quotes.speaker: Judas Iscariot
quotes.context: At the Passover meal after Jesus said one of the twelve would betray him. Jesus answered, 'You have said so.'

quotes.text: Though they all fall away because of you, I will never fall away.
quotes.speaker: Peter
quotes.context: On the way to the Mount of Olives, after Jesus said all would fall away that night. Jesus foretold he would deny him three times.

quotes.text: My Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will, but as you will.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: Praying in Gethsemane with his face on the ground, the first of three prayers.

quotes.text: So, could you not watch with me one hour?
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To Peter, on finding the disciples asleep in Gethsemane.

quotes.text: The one I will kiss is the man; seize him.
quotes.speaker: Judas Iscariot (the betrayer)
quotes.context: The sign he gave the crowd with swords and clubs sent by the chief priests. He then said 'Greetings, Rabbi!' and kissed Jesus.

quotes.text: Friend, do what you came to do.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: To Judas, after Judas greeted and kissed him in Gethsemane.

quotes.text: Put your sword back into its place. For all who take the sword will perish by the sword.
quotes.speaker: Jesus
quotes.context: After one of his disciples cut off the ear of the high priest's servant at the arrest.

quotes.text: I adjure you by the living God, tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God.
quotes.speaker: The high priest (Caiaphas)
quotes.context: At Jesus' trial before the council, after Jesus stayed silent at the false testimony.

quotes.text: He has uttered blasphemy. What further witnesses do we need?
quotes.speaker: The high priest (Caiaphas)
quotes.context: Tearing his robes after Jesus said they would see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power.

quotes.text: Prophesy to us, you Christ! Who is it that struck you?
quotes.speaker: Members of the council and those with them
quotes.context: Mocking Jesus while spitting on him and striking him after he was condemned.

quotes.text: You also were with Jesus the Galilean.
quotes.speaker: A servant girl
quotes.context: To Peter as he sat outside in the courtyard of the high priest; the first of his three denials followed.

quotes.text: Certainly you too are one of them, for your accent betrays you.
quotes.speaker: The bystanders
quotes.context: To Peter in the high priest's courtyard, leading to his third denial and the rooster crowing.

quotes.text: I do not know the man.
quotes.speaker: Peter
quotes.context: His third denial, with cursing and swearing, in the high priest's courtyard; immediately the rooster crowed.

quotes.text: I have sinned by betraying innocent blood.
quotes.speaker: Judas Iscariot
quotes.context: Bringing back the thirty pieces of silver after Jesus was condemned. The chief priests replied, 'What is that to us? See to it yourself.'

quotes.text: Are you the King of the Jews?
quotes.speaker: Pontius Pilate, the governor
quotes.context: Questioning Jesus; Jesus answered, 'You have said so,' and gave no answer to the chief priests' accusations.

quotes.text: Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered much because of him today in a dream.
quotes.speaker: Pilate's wife
quotes.context: A message sent to Pilate while he was sitting on the judgment seat, deciding between Jesus and Barabbas.

quotes.text: Let him be crucified!
quotes.speaker: The crowd
quotes.context: When Pilate asked, 'Then what shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?' after they chose Barabbas.

quotes.text: I am innocent of this man's blood; see to it yourselves.
quotes.speaker: Pontius Pilate
quotes.context: Washing his hands before the crowd when he saw a riot was beginning.

quotes.text: His blood be on us and on our children!
quotes.speaker: All the people (the crowd)
quotes.context: Responding to Pilate after he washed his hands of Jesus' blood.

quotes.text: Hail, King of the Jews!
quotes.speaker: The governor's soldiers
quotes.context: Mocking Jesus in the governor's headquarters after dressing him in a scarlet robe with a crown of thorns and a reed.

quotes.text: He saved others; he cannot save himself. He is the King of Israel; let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him.
quotes.speaker: The chief priests, with the scribes and elders
quotes.context: Mocking Jesus as he hung on the cross at Golgotha.

quotes.text: Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?
quotes.speaker: Jesus (quoting Psalm 22)
quotes.context: Crying out with a loud voice about the ninth hour on the cross, after three hours of darkness. It means 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'

quotes.text: This man is calling Elijah.
quotes.speaker: Some of the bystanders at the cross
quotes.context: Misunderstanding Jesus' cry 'Eli, Eli'; one ran to offer him sour wine on a sponge.

quotes.text: Truly this was the Son of God!
quotes.speaker: The centurion and those with him keeping watch over Jesus
quotes.context: Filled with awe at the earthquake and what took place when Jesus died.

quotes.text: Sir, we remember how that impostor said, while he was still alive, 'After three days I will rise.'
quotes.speaker: The chief priests and the Pharisees
quotes.context: Asking Pilate the day after the crucifixion to make the tomb secure, so the disciples would not steal the body.

quotes.text: You have a guard of soldiers. Go, make it as secure as you can.
quotes.speaker: Pontius Pilate
quotes.context: To the chief priests and Pharisees, who then sealed the stone and set a guard.

quotes.text: He is not here, for he has risen, as he said. Come, see the place where he lay.
quotes.speaker: An angel of the Lord
quotes.context: Sitting on the stone rolled away from the tomb, speaking to Mary Magdalene and the other Mary.

quotes.text: Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they will see me.
quotes.speaker: Jesus (risen)
quotes.context: Meeting the women as they ran from the empty tomb; they took hold of his feet and worshiped him.

quotes.text: Tell people, 'His disciples came by night and stole him away while we were asleep.'
quotes.speaker: The chief priests and elders
quotes.context: Bribing the soldiers of the guard with a sufficient sum of money after the resurrection.

quotes.text: Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name? ... I never knew you; depart from me, you workers of lawlessness.
quotes.speaker: Many who call Jesus 'Lord' on that day, then Jesus
quotes.context: Sermon on the Mount: not everyone who says 'Lord, Lord' will enter the kingdom, but the one who does the Father's will.

quotes.text: Lord, have mercy on my son, for he has seizures and he suffers terribly. For often he falls into the fire, and often into the water.
quotes.speaker: A father (a man kneeling before Jesus)
quotes.context: After Jesus came down from the mount of Transfiguration; the disciples had not been able to heal the boy.

quotes.text: Lord, lord, open to us. ... Truly, I say to you, I do not know you.
quotes.speaker: The five foolish virgins, then the bridegroom
quotes.context: In the parable of the ten virgins, after the door was shut while the foolish were away buying oil.

verses.text: She will bear a son, and you shall call his name [[Jesus]], for he will save his people from their [[sins]].
Behold, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall call his name [[Immanuel]] (which means, God with us).
And you, O [[Bethlehem]], in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.
Then, opening their treasures, they offered him gifts, [[gold and frankincense and myrrh]].
The voice of one crying in the [[wilderness]]: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.'
I baptize you with water for repentance, but he who is coming after me is mightier than I... He will baptize you with the [[Holy Spirit and fire]].
Man shall not live by [[bread]] alone, but by every [[word]] that comes from the mouth of God.
Be gone, Satan! For it is written, 'You shall [[worship]] the Lord your God and him only shall you serve.'
Follow me, and I will make you [[fishers of men]].
Blessed are the [[poor in spirit]], for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are those who [[mourn]], for they shall be [[comforted]].
Blessed are the [[meek]], for they shall inherit the [[earth]].
Blessed are those who [[hunger and thirst for righteousness]], for they shall be satisfied.
Blessed are the [[merciful]], for they shall receive mercy.
Blessed are the [[pure in heart]], for they shall see God.
Blessed are the [[peacemakers]], for they shall be called [[sons of God]].
You are the [[salt]] of the earth, but if salt has lost its taste, how shall its saltiness be restored?
You are the [[light of the world]]. A city set on a [[hill]] cannot be hidden.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your [[good works]] and give glory to your [[Father]] who is in heaven.
Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to [[fulfill]] them.
But I say to you, Do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, [[turn to him the other also]].
But I say to you, [[Love your enemies]] and [[pray for those who persecute you]].
You therefore must be [[perfect]], as your heavenly Father is perfect.
But when you give to the needy, do not let your [[left hand]] know what your [[right hand]] is doing.
Our Father in heaven, [[hallowed be your name]]. Your kingdom come, your [[will]] be done, on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our [[daily bread]], and forgive us our [[debts]], as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into [[temptation]], but deliver us from evil.
Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where [[moth and rust]] destroy and where thieves break in and steal, but lay up for yourselves treasures in [[heaven]].
For where your [[treasure]] is, there your [[heart]] will be also.
No one can serve [[two masters]], for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and [[money]].
Look at the [[birds of the air]]: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they?
Consider the [[lilies of the field]], how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, yet I tell you, even [[Solomon]] in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
But seek first the [[kingdom of God]] and his [[righteousness]], and all these things will be added to you.
Therefore do not be anxious about [[tomorrow]], for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Sufficient for the day is its own [[trouble]].
[[Judge not]], that you be not judged.
Why do you see the [[speck]] that is in your brother's eye, but do not notice the [[log]] that is in your own eye?
Do not give dogs what is holy, and do not throw your [[pearls]] before [[pigs]], lest they trample them underfoot and turn to attack you.
[[Ask]], and it will be given to you; [[seek]], and you will find; [[knock]], and it will be opened to you.
So whatever you wish that others would do to you, [[do also to them]], for this is the [[Law and the Prophets]].

Enter by the [[narrow gate]]. For the gate is wide and the way is easy that leads to [[destruction]], and those who enter by it are many. For the gate is narrow and the way is hard that leads to life, and those who find it are few.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in [[sheep's clothing]] but inwardly are ravenous [[wolves]].
Thus you will recognize them by their [[fruits]].
Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the [[rock]].
Those who are well have no need of a [[physician]], but those who are [[sick]].
Go and learn what this means: 'I desire [[mercy]], and not [[sacrifice]].' For I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.
Neither is new wine put into old [[wineskins]]. If it is, the skins burst and the wine is spilled and the skins are destroyed.
The [[harvest]] is plentiful, but the [[laborers]] are few; therefore pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.
Behold, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves, so be wise as [[serpents]] and innocent as [[doves]].
And do not fear those who kill the [[body]] but cannot kill the [[soul]]. Rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
Are not two [[sparrows]] sold for a penny? And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father. But even the [[hairs of your head]] are all numbered.
Do not think that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I have not come to bring peace, but a [[sword]].
Whoever finds his life will [[lose]] it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will [[find]] it.
Come to me, all who [[labor]] and are [[heavy laden]], and I will give you rest.
Take my [[yoke]] upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. For my yoke is [[easy]], and my burden is [[light]].
For the Son of Man is lord of the [[Sabbath]].
Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or [[house divided against itself]] will stand.
Whoever is not with me is [[against me]], and whoever does not gather with me [[scatters]].
For out of the abundance of the [[heart]] the [[mouth]] speaks.
For just as [[Jonah]] was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so will the Son of Man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
For whoever does the [[will of my Father]] in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.

The kingdom of heaven is like a grain of [[mustard seed]] that a man took and sowed in his field. It is the smallest of all seeds, but when it has grown it is larger than all the garden plants and becomes a [[tree]].
The kingdom of heaven is like [[treasure hidden in a field]], which a man found and covered up. Then in his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls, who, on finding one [[pearl of great value]], went and sold all that he had and bought it.
A prophet is not without [[honor]] except in his [[hometown]] and in his own household.
This people honors me with their [[lips]], but their [[heart]] is far from me.
It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what [[comes out of the mouth]]; this defiles a person.
They are blind guides. And if the [[blind]] lead the blind, both will fall into a [[pit]].
And I tell you, you are [[Peter]], and on this [[rock]] I will build my [[church]], and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
I will give you the [[keys of the kingdom of heaven]], and whatever you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven.
If anyone would come after me, let him [[deny himself]] and take up his [[cross]] and follow me.
For what will it profit a man if he gains the whole [[world]] and forfeits his [[soul]]?
For truly, I say to you, if you have faith like a grain of [[mustard seed]], you will say to this [[mountain]], 'Move from here to there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you.
Truly, I say to you, unless you turn and become like [[children]], you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
If a man has a hundred sheep, and one of them has gone astray, does he not leave the [[ninety-nine]] on the mountains and go in search of the one that went astray?
For where [[two or three]] are gathered in my name, there am I among them.
I do not say to you seven times, but [[seventy-seven]] times. (ESV footnote: or seventy times seven)
So they are no longer two but [[one flesh]]. What therefore God has joined together, let not man [[separate]].
Let the [[little children]] come to me and do not hinder them, for to such belongs the kingdom of heaven.
Again I tell you, it is easier for a [[camel]] to go through the eye of a [[needle]] than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.
With man this is impossible, but with God [[all things are possible]].
So the [[last]] will be first, and the [[first]] last.
Even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to [[serve]], and to give his life as a [[ransom]] for many.
[[Hosanna]] to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the [[name of the Lord]]! Hosanna in the highest!
It is written, 'My house shall be called a house of [[prayer]],' but you make it a [[den of robbers]].
And whatever you ask in prayer, you will receive, if you have [[faith]].
The stone that the builders [[rejected]] has become the [[cornerstone]].
For many are [[called]], but few are [[chosen]].
Therefore render to [[Caesar]] the things that are Caesar's, and to [[God]] the things that are God's.
You shall love the Lord your God with all your [[heart]] and with all your [[soul]] and with all your [[mind]].
And a second is like it: You shall love your [[neighbor]] as [[yourself]]. On these two commandments depend all the Law and the Prophets.
The greatest among you shall be your [[servant]]. Whoever exalts himself will be [[humbled]], and whoever humbles himself will be [[exalted]].
You blind guides, straining out a [[gnat]] and swallowing a [[camel]]!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like [[whitewashed tombs]], which outwardly appear beautiful, but within are full of dead people's bones and all uncleanness.
And this gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world as a testimony to [[all nations]], and then the [[end]] will come.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my [[words]] will not pass away.
But concerning that day and hour [[no one knows]], not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son, but the [[Father]] only.
For as were the days of [[Noah]], so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Watch therefore, for you know neither the [[day]] nor the [[hour]].
Well done, [[good and faithful]] servant. You have been faithful over a [[little]]; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master.

For I was [[hungry]] and you gave me food, I was [[thirsty]] and you gave me drink, I was a [[stranger]] and you welcomed me, I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in [[prison]] and you came to me.
Truly, I say to you, as you did it to one of the [[least of these]] my brothers, you did it to [[me]].
Take, eat; this is my [[body]].
For this is my blood of the [[covenant]], which is poured out for many for the [[forgiveness of sins]].
Truly, I tell you, this very night, before the [[rooster]] crows, you will deny me [[three times]].
My Father, if it be possible, let this [[cup]] pass from me; nevertheless, not as [[I will]], but as [[you will]].
Watch and pray that you may not enter into temptation. The [[spirit]] indeed is willing, but the [[flesh]] is weak.
Put your sword back into its place. For all who take the [[sword]] will [[perish]] by the sword.
Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani? that is, My God, my God, why have you [[forsaken]] me?
Truly this was the [[Son of God]]!
He is not here, for he has [[risen]], as he said. Come, see the place where he [[lay]].
[[All authority]] in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
Go therefore and make [[disciples]] of [[all nations]], baptizing them in the name of the [[Father]] and of the [[Son]] and of the [[Holy Spirit]].
Teaching them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you [[always]], to the [[end of the age]].

names.name: Jesus
names.note: Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham; the Messiah, Immanuel.

names.name: Abraham
names.note: Patriarch; the genealogy begins with him; God is 'the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob'.

names.name: David
names.note: King; Jesus is called 'Son of David'; ate the bread of the Presence; calls the Christ 'Lord' in Psalm 110.

names.name: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and 'the wife of Uriah' (Bathsheba)
names.note: The four women from the Old Testament named in Jesus' genealogy.

names.name: Zerubbabel
names.note: Named in the genealogy after the deportation to Babylon.

names.name: Mary
names.note: Mother of Jesus, betrothed to Joseph; found with child from the Holy Spirit.

names.name: Joseph (husband of Mary)
names.note: A just man; obeys four dreams (take Mary, flee to Egypt, return, go to Galilee).

names.name: Herod the Great (King Herod)
names.note: Troubled by the Magi; kills the children of Bethlehem; dies while Jesus is in Egypt.

names.name: The wise men (Magi)
names.note: From the east; follow the star; bring gold, frankincense and myrrh.

names.name: Archelaus
names.note: Herod's son who reigned over Judea, so Joseph went to Galilee instead.

names.name: Rachel
names.note: 'Rachel weeping for her children' (Jeremiah) fulfilled in the killing of the children.

names.name: John the Baptist
names.note: Forerunner; baptizes in the Jordan; imprisoned and beheaded by Herod the tetrarch; the 'Elijah who is to come'.

names.name: The devil (Satan, the tempter)
names.note: Tempts Jesus in the wilderness; Jesus later says 'Get behind me, Satan' to Peter.

names.name: Simon Peter
names.note: Fisherman, first-named apostle; walks on water, confesses Jesus as the Christ, sees the Transfiguration, denies Jesus three times.

names.name: Andrew
names.note: Peter's brother, fisherman, called with him.

names.name: James and John, sons of Zebedee
names.note: Fishermen called from their father's boat; at the Transfiguration and Gethsemane; their mother asks for places of honor.

names.name: Matthew
names.note: Tax collector called from the tax booth; listed as 'Matthew the tax collector' among the twelve.

names.name: Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot
names.note: The other members of the twelve.

names.name: Judas Iscariot
names.note: The apostle who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver with a kiss, then hanged himself.

names.name: Herod the tetrarch (Herod Antipas)
names.note: Beheads John the Baptist; thinks Jesus is John raised from the dead.

names.name: Herodias and her daughter
names.note: Herodias, wife of Herod's brother Philip; her daughter dances and asks for John's head.

names.name: The centurion of Capernaum
names.note: Gentile officer whose faith Jesus marvels at.

names.name: The Canaanite woman
names.note: Woman from the region of Tyre and Sidon whose great faith heals her daughter.

names.name: Moses and Elijah
names.note: Appear with Jesus at the Transfiguration; Elijah is identified with John the Baptist.

names.name: Jonah
names.note: The 'sign of Jonah': three days and three nights in the great fish; Nineveh repented.

names.name: The queen of the South and Solomon
names.note: She came to hear Solomon's wisdom; 'something greater than Solomon is here'. Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like the lilies.

names.name: Isaiah
names.note: The prophet most often quoted in Matthew (the voice in the wilderness, the light in Galilee, the chosen servant, hearts far away).

names.name: Jeremiah
names.note: Quoted about Rachel weeping and the thirty pieces of silver; some think Jesus is Jeremiah.

names.name: Daniel
names.note: Prophet who spoke of the 'abomination of desolation'.

names.name: Noah
names.note: The coming of the Son of Man will be like the days of Noah.

names.name: Abel and Zechariah son of Barachiah
names.note: Righteous blood shed from Abel to Zechariah, murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.

names.name: Beelzebul
names.note: 'Prince of demons'; the Pharisees claim Jesus casts out demons by him.

names.name: Caiaphas
names.note: High priest; the plot is made at his palace; he puts Jesus under oath and tears his robes.

names.name: Simon the leper
names.note: Owner of the house in Bethany where Jesus is anointed.

names.name: Pontius Pilate
names.note: Roman governor; releases Barabbas, washes his hands, grants the guard at the tomb.

names.name: Pilate's wife
names.note: Warns Pilate because of a dream about 'that righteous man'.

names.name: Barabbas
names.note: A notorious prisoner released instead of Jesus.

names.name: Simon of Cyrene
names.note: Compelled to carry Jesus' cross.

names.name: Mary Magdalene and 'the other Mary'
names.note: Watch the crucifixion and burial; first to the empty tomb and to meet the risen Jesus.

names.name: Joseph of Arimathea
names.note: Rich man and disciple who buries Jesus in his own new tomb.

names.name: Bethlehem
names.note: Town of Judea where Jesus is born (Micah's prophecy).

names.name: Egypt
names.note: Where the family flees from Herod ('Out of Egypt I called my son').

names.name: Nazareth
names.note: Jesus' hometown in Galilee ('He shall be called a Nazarene'); where he was rejected.

names.name: The Jordan River
names.note: Where John baptizes and Jesus is baptized.

names.name: Galilee and the Sea of Galilee
names.note: Region of most of Jesus' ministry; where the first disciples were fishing; where the risen Jesus meets the eleven.

names.name: Capernaum
names.note: Jesus' home base by the sea; home of the centurion; rebuked as unrepentant.

names.name: Country of the Gadarenes
names.note: Where two demoniacs are healed and the pigs rush into the sea.

names.name: Chorazin and Bethsaida
names.note: Unrepentant cities Jesus pronounces woes on.

names.name: Tyre and Sidon; Sodom
names.note: Would have repented had they seen Jesus' works; Jesus meets the Canaanite woman in the district of Tyre and Sidon.

names.name: Gennesaret
names.note: Where the sick touch the fringe of his garment and are healed.

names.name: Magadan
names.note: Region Jesus goes to by boat after feeding the four thousand.

names.name: Caesarea Philippi
names.note: Where Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ.

names.name: Jericho
names.note: Leaving it, Jesus heals two blind men.

names.name: Bethphage and the Mount of Olives
names.note: Where the donkey is found; setting of the Olivet Discourse and Jesus' walk to Gethsemane.

names.name: Bethany
names.note: Where Jesus lodges and is anointed at Simon the leper's house.

names.name: Gethsemane
names.note: Where Jesus prays and is arrested.

names.name: The Field of Blood (the potter's field)
names.note: Bought with Judas's thirty pieces of silver as a burial place for strangers.

names.name: Golgotha ('Place of a Skull')
names.note: Where Jesus is crucified.
